author: Darrell Hofheinz
title: Neighbor linked to $28M purchase of neglected house in Palm Beach - NewsBreak
text:
By Darrell Hofheinz ,
1 days ago Public records link the buyer of a recently landmarked 1930s-era oceanside house in Palm Beach to another landmarked home immediately behind the property.
A deed recorded March 9 shows the buyer who paid $28 million for 480 S. Ocean Blvd. is a New York-registered limited liability company with the same mailing address as the Peter R. & Cynthia K. Kellogg Foundation in New York City. The foundation is the charitable arm of the family of Peter Kellogg, a billionaire who made his fortune on Wall Street and in the reinsurance industry.
Cynthia Kellogg is listed in property records as one of the two owners of a house at 17 Middle Road, immediately west of the one that just changed hands. She co-owns the Middle Road house with her daughter, Lee Kellogg Sadrian, property records show. Lee Sadrian also is the namesake of a charitable foundation, the Justin & Lee Kellogg Sadrian Foundation.
The house that changed hands at 480 S. Ocean Blvd. drew attention last year after it sat empty for months with its windows boarded up and its lawn overgrown in the wake a renovation project that had come to an abrupt halt following the 2024 death of its longtime owner, Patricia Ann Kahn. The neglected condition of the house sparked a code-enforcement complaint after the property became an eyesore in the Estate Section neighborhood.
The buyer listed on the deed was E and A Property Holdings LLC. According to town records, people on the buyer's side plan to complete the renovation in accordance with the town's landmarks process.
Built in 1935, the house was sold by the estate of Kahn, who died Aug. 24, 2024, at 89 .
The traditional-style, four-bedroom house has 6,097 square feet of living space, inside and out. On a lot of about three-quarters of an acre, the house stands a little less than a quarter-mile south of Worth Avenue. The property’s narrow beach parcel runs along the opposite side of the coastal road.
The house had been under contract since July, according to records in the multiple listing service.
Agent Stephen Ploof of Compass Florida in Palm Beach was one of two agents on the seller's side of the transaction. The property entered the market with a price tag of $38.65 million in March 2025, when Ploof was affiliated with the old Hilton Hilton agency. He co-listed the estate with Miami-based agent Natalia Gryczynska of Serhant.
Ploof and Gryczynska declined to comment about the sale.
Agent Missy Savage of Brown Harris Stevens in Palm Beach handled the buyer's side of the sale, the multiple listing service shows. She had no comment about the sale and said her clients, whom she did not identify, would not discuss the transaction.
In July, a Town Hall staff member told members of the Code Enforcement Board that the waiting-in-the-wings buyer planned to finish the renovation and supported a move to designate it a town landmark.
The Town Council granted the house landmark status in Novembe r. The designation generally prevents the exteriors of structures deemed landmarks from being significantly altered without the permission of the Landmarks Preservation Commission.
The property had drawn the code board’s attention after an April 2025 inspection showed its neglected condition — with windows open to the elements — along with missing construction screening and a general lack of landscaping.
Kahn's name had been associated with the house’s ownership since at least 1984, although courthouse records provide no indication of any amount changing hands at that time.
At the July code board meeting, board members leveled a $125 administration fee but delayed the imposition of any fines related to the condition of the property after being told a deal was in the works to sell it.
“We’ve been in conversations with the buyer who has the house in contract, and they are aware of the landmarking process and are enthusiastic about working within the parameters,” Friederike Mittner, the town’s design and preservation manager, told the code board. She did not identify the buyer by name.
The board extended its deadline for the property to be brought into compliance with the portion of the town’s code requiring the exterior of the house to be maintained in “good repair” and meet standards so that it is “structurally sound.”
The late Palm Beach architect Marion Sims Wyeth designed the house in the Monterey style, incorporating British Colonial and “early Palm Beach” architectural influences, according to a report prepared as part of the landmarking process.
Following last April's code inspection, conditions improved at the property, with openings boarded up, construction screening installed and gravel spread on the ground to reduce dust, attorney Paul Minoff, representing the seller, told the code board last year.
Kahn’s obituary described her as a singer who performed in nightclubs for 25 years and who had a passion for traveling.
The house was commissioned 91 years ago by longtime seasonal Palm Beach visitor and, later, resident Helen Bird Johnson Bolton Fitzgerald, who was married twice, according to the landmarks report. Her first husband was Harlan Kent Bolton, a member of one the town’s oldest families; and her second was Harold Fitzgerald of Massachusetts and New York City.
Helen Fitzgerald entertained frequently at the Palm Beach house until her death in 1969, the report says. The property was then purchased by the late Esther and Allen Ransom of Michigan and Illinois, before Kahn obtained it.
The house owned by Cynthia Kellogg and Lee Kellogg Sadrian on Middle Road was landmarked in 2015 , town records show. Built in 1934, it was designed by Treanor & Fatio — the firm of noted society architect Maurice Fatio — and features Colonial Revival-style architecture with British Colonial influences.
Peter Kellogg is chairman and former CEO of IAT Reinsurance Group. In 2000, he sold Spear, Leeds & Kellogg, a brokerage company, to Goldman Sachs for $6.5 billion in cash and stock, according to published reports. Forbes.com estimates his net worth at $5.3 billion.
Justin Sadrian is managing director and co-head of U.S. technology at Warburg Pincus, a private-equity firm headquartered in New York City.
Patricia A. Mitulinsky, vice president and trust real estate advisor at PNC Bank, signed the deed to sell the house on South Ocean Boulevard. The bank is the personal representative of Kahn's estate and trustee of a trust in her name, the deed shows.
Darrell Hofheinz is a USA TODAY Network of Florida journalist who writes about Palm Beach real estate in his weekly “Beyond the Hedges” column. He welcomes tips about real estate news on the island.
